summary.intent: Coordinate review-fix work across multiple PRs (#343, #347, and a #367/#348/#349 worker), driving worker agents to resolve review findings and get CI and Entire Gates passing.
summary.outcome: PR #343 is complete and verified (all checks passed, 0 open findings). PR #347 has round 4 pushed with a structural scoping fix for same-name interfaces/type aliases, but CI and Entire Gates were still pending, so its findings are not final.

repo: Review findings are read with `entire trail finding list caliper/144 --project gh/orin-dx --freshness current --status open --json`. A '0 open findings' result is only valid after Entire Gates completes.

CI state is checked with `gh pr checks <PR>`. 347 has 16 non-Entire checks (Audit, Changesets, Coverage, Install Node 24/26 with npm/pnpm, Lint, MSRV, SemVer, Native binding crate tests, Python scripts, Rust, TypeScript Node 24/26, Vite plugin).

Local verification commands: `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core`, `just lint doc-check machete typos`, and a clean-room worktree with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` plus `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

`scripts/interface_scope_oracle.mjs [N]` checks the extractor against TypeScript 6.0.3's checker (from `apps/oracle`). It runs the ignored Rust test `extractor::tests::interface_scopes_match_typescript`.
Registry keys for interfaces and type aliases now carry scope as `file:Name@<body start offset>`. Module-level keys are unchanged, and both kinds use `declared_type_key`.

code.finding: Holds `TypeFrame` and the scope-key helpers. Function bodies, blocks, static blocks and switches that declare interfaces or type aliases are their own scope.
`record_result_of` re-enters the body's scope so factory results through a local interface or alias still resolve.
Enums and classes are still keyed by bare name here. They are also values reached through value paths, so a function-local one can collide with a module-level one.
Another site that keys classes or enums by bare name and was not converted to scoped keys.
Bare-name keying site, left unchanged along with `pending_classes` and the `visit.rs` enum visitor.

workflow: Validate a fix by stashing the source changes and running the new tests against the old source. All three new tests failed there, which shows they exercise the fix.
An oracle test against the language's own checker (TypeScript here) enumerates scope combinations exhaustively. It exposed 72 of 84 mismatches at N=3 before the fix and 0 of 340 at N=4 after.
A review result read before the gating check completes is provisional, not final.

friction: CI and Entire Gates on 347 sat unchanged in IN_PROGRESS or QUEUED for about 15 minutes of polling, so the worker had to stop without a final result.
The 0-open-findings reading on 347 came before Entire Gates finished, so it can't be trusted.
The oracle expansion enlarged PR 347 by about 466 lines beyond what the original finding asked for.
open_items: After Entire Gates completes on 6f558c30, re-run the finding list for caliper/144 and read each non-Entire check by name.
Follow up on the bare-name keying of enums and classes, where a function-local one can collide with a module-level one. This collision is untested and the oracle doesn't cover it.
Add namespace-in-function cases to the oracle.
Decide whether the oracle script and its ignored Rust test (about 466 added lines) stay in PR 347.
The #367/#348/#349 worker is still running and needs to be checked.
PR 343 had no changeset from its worker. One was added on a separate branch earlier.
